<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 46 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6539ce3c6c5b6c550a1d9079b6616afd0da0126e` — the merge of head `af275005b9f3e440c75ebcd4ee2f509eb2d8fecd` into base `d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6539ce3c6c5b6c550a1d9079b6616afd0da0126e && git checkout 6539ce3c6c5b6c550a1d9079b6616afd0da0126e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726 af275005b9f3e440c75ebcd4ee2f509eb2d8fecd && git checkout -B drift-repro d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726 && git merge --no-ff af275005b9f3e440c75ebcd4ee2f509eb2d8fecd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：凡是"主从"关系的子表（比如报价单的明细行），在父记录详情页里默认显示为正文里的表格，排在基本信息上方，带服务器算的合计、默认 10 行、「显示全部」和跳转按钮；不再是右侧的小卡片。想保持原样的，在子表字段上写「显示为侧边列表」即可。
- 为什么做：记录详情页重做专题的一张卡，按您说的「就是 master-detail 表类型的子表」，改为按关系类型决定，不再要求"可在表单内编辑"。
- 出错会怎样：所有现有应用的主从子表都会换到正文位置；如果排版有问题，影响面是所有带主从子表的详情页。合计来自服务器，不会只算当前看到的几行。
- 要你做什么：这次改了架构决策记录（ADR-0035），需要您或指定审批人人工合并；席位先做合同复审。
- 席位意见：通过，只差一处补登记（文字即可）；建议合并前补一组真实界面截图，因为所有带主从子表的详情页都会变。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT, one text-only item** · head `b4ba2a6df69aa874c2ecbc3d3bc2e2b201549a8f` · Fixes #35597 (epic #35590, maintainer direct dispatch cited in claim 7023261217) · K=4 · merge-tree clean · **GOVERNED: `docs/adr/0035-config-driven-master-detail.md`, Tier H** · 1,290 lines · CI 61 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed · 2026-11-20T00:14Z

**The predicate change.** `isBodyTableRelationship` now answers `field.type === 'master_detail'` when no `relatedList` is declared. Before, it also required `inlineEdit ∈ {true, 'grid', 'form'}`. `relatedList: false`, `true` and `'primary'` answer as before, and a `lookup` with no `relatedList` stays a side card. The refusal text loses only the `inlineEdit` clause.

**Clause-② yes (widening): holds, and no narrowing.** At `defineStack` and at the publish door, a field group may now name a plain `master_detail` child that used to be refused as a side card. Nothing accepted before is refused now: the refused cases that remain, a hidden list and `relatedList: false`, were refused before too. The pins move accordingly:
- `stack-related-lists-order.test.ts` swaps its refusal case to `relatedList: false`;
- the protocol save-door CONTROL fixture now says `relatedList: true`;
- the lint rule gains an accepted plain-`master_detail` case.

**Existing apps: disclosed.** Every parent whose `master_detail` children declare no `relatedList` changes its record page: the side card becomes a body table above the field sections. The changeset says so and gives the way back (`relatedList: true` on the FK), with spec, plugin-detail and app-shell graded minor.

**Totals: server-owned, as ADR-0035 binds.** Server totals come from the parent's `summary` roll-up when it sums the same rows, otherwise from `dataSource.aggregate` over the list's own condition. There is no client sum. Pins: `RelatedList.bodyTable-27055.test.tsx` has 15 cells, including "total over EVERY row, not the rows on show", "no aggregate ⇒ no totals", "a roll-up with its own filter is not this list's total" (CONTROL) and record-mode currency grouping. `deriveRelatedLists` and `authoredBodyTableIds` have CONTROLs too.

**ADR.** The amendment block is add-only. The one removed line is the Status line, which gains an `**Amended** (2026-11-19, #35597…)` marker; the word-diff shows nothing else on it changing. It is in its own commit, `d4364f43`, as the claim says. The seat ruled the override of ruling B (#27478) authorised.

**R1 (text only, no push, no fresh L1): claim amendment for the files outside claim 7023261217's surface.**
- **Spec sources:** `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (the `relatedList` jsdoc and describe) and `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (the field-group jsdoc and describe). These are published describes, so name them.
- **Tests of fenced or other packages:**
  - `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/RecordPageColumns.test.tsx` (`RecordPageColumns.tsx` is ⛔);
  - `packages/lint/src/validate-related-list-refs.test.ts`;
  - `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`;
  - `packages/spec/src/stack-related-lists-order.test.ts`;
  - `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ObjectFieldInspector.relatedList-27054.test.tsx`;
  - `RelatedList.parentCurrency-31912.test.tsx`;
  - `record-related-list.emptyFold-25895.test.tsx`.
  These are the "side-list fixtures in a few out-of-surface tests" the relay names.
- The generated reference pages fall under "the generated spec baselines it moves".

**Nit (for the L2).** The `relatedList` describe still opens "true/absent = shown as an auxiliary panel" and only later says "Absent on a master_detail field, the list is 'primary' by default". The first clause now reads wrong for `master_detail`; "true (and absent on a lookup)" would match.

**Recommended before the human merge (not an L1 item).** The A4 browser reading was not measured. This changes the face of every record page with `master_detail` children in every app. One CRM or showcase pass would show the approver the new layout: a quote with line items, an empty child, and a child over 10 rows. The checklist item `records-forms.master-detail-body-tables` carries the live legs.

**Routing.** Clause-② yes (widening) on `packages/spec`: L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` by seat 5. Then **Tier H** for the ADR path: the maintainer's merge, or an APPROVED review from GOVERNED_APPROVERS (os-zhuang / hotlong) followed by the seat's landing. Skills text follow-up #35692 is filed and blocked by this card.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b4ba2a6df69aa874c2ecbc3d3bc2e2b201549a8f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/related-list-body-table.ts, docs/adr/0035-config-driven-master-detail.md + ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx
Security-touching: no

PR #35691, card #35597. Read: the card body and its four comments (triage, claim, section notice 7023388416, dev report), the PR body, the 29-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head (every run success or skipped, none failed). The epic #35590 is not an input of this review, so the maintainer's words are checked against the card body only.

### ① Derived judgments

- `isBodyTableRelationship`: one verdict cell moves. A `master_detail` FK with no `relatedList` and no `inlineEdit` (absent or `false`) was a side list and is a body table. `relatedList: 'primary'` stays body, `true` stays side, `false` stays hidden, a `lookup` with no `relatedList` stays side, any other field type stays `false`. **Right** against card rule 1, cell by cell.
- `fieldGroupBodyTableRefusal`, at `defineStack` and at the publish door through `@objectstack/lint`: the accept set **widens**. A field group may name a plain `master_detail` child. Because the body set only grows, no group that parsed or published before is refused now. **Right**, and it follows from the one predicate with no second copy. The metadata-protocol test fixture moving to `relatedList: true` confirms the runtime door follows.
- Nothing narrows. Every consumer of the predicate at this head was read (`stack.zod.ts`, `validate-related-list-refs.ts`, `deriveRelatedLists.ts`, `RecordDetailView.tsx`, both Studio inspectors): none refuses a relationship for being a body table, so the widened predicate takes nothing away from an author.
- `RelatedListRelationshipFields.inlineEdit` stays on the exported interface and is no longer read. **Right**: the public type does not move, and a caller may still hand over the whole field.
- `FieldSchema.relatedList` and `ObjectFieldGroupSchema.relatedList`: the parse accept sets are unchanged (`boolean | 'primary'`; the entry pattern). The meaning of an omitted `relatedList` on a `master_detail` FK changes. **Right** as a changed default.
- Stored metadata: no rewrite and no conversion. A stored object with a plain `master_detail` FK draws its child in the overview after upgrade; the opt-out is `relatedList: true`, and the changeset says so. **Right** for a changed default, which ruling A does not treat as a break.
- New UI export `authoredBodyTableIds` (app-shell). The client sum "Totals (this page)" is removed and replaced by server totals. **Right** against card rules 5 and 7.
- Owed, outside the diff and not graded: the shipped D3 entry `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.field-group-related-list-side-card-refused.ts` still lists "a plain master_detail with no inlineEdit" among the refused shapes and quotes the old predicate in its reason. After this PR, `os migrate meta` prints a notice for a shape that is accepted. The dev's list of stale comments does not name it. A follow-up card should cover it.

### ② Semver level

The kind is `semantic`, and that is the right word from the closed vocabulary (added / narrowed / semantic / none, AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). The diff carries two protocol facts: a changed default (an omitted `relatedList` on a `master_detail` FK), which is `semantic`, and a newly accepted value at the field-group check, which is `added`. Nothing is narrowed (see ①). The precedence rule puts `semantic` over `added`. The claim's "widened" is not in the vocabulary, and the dev was right to replace it.

The level follows the kind: at least `minor` on every package the diff moves. The changeset takes `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and `@object-ui/app-shell`, which are exactly the three packages with non-test source in the diff. `packages/lint` and `packages/metadata-protocol` change tests only and publish nothing. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed for this kind.

The Clause-② line reads `yes (widening)` in the PR body and `yes (widening: …)` in the changeset. The reader takes the first token inside the parenthesis as the arm, so both read the same value and the same arm, and the Metadata-protocol line is present and identical in both. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, each answered:

- Kind declared `semantic`, not the order's "widened": accepted, see ②.
- No new i18n keys, four existing keys reused: accepted; a lane matter.
- Tests of fenced sources edited for fixtures only: lane seat's ACCEPT; the fenced sources themselves are not in the file list.
- `RelatedList.tsx` edits run past the claimed line range: accepted. Every hunk is gated on `bodyTable` or lives inside the totals hook. For a list that is not a body table, `effectivePageSize`, the pager and the New button compute as before.
- Stale comments left outside the surface: accepted as follow-up, together with the D3 entry named in ①.
- The section comment on the card: as ordered.
- `open_questions`: none.

Questions put to this review:

- **New server aggregate path: none.** The file list holds no server source. The totals call the data source's existing spec-shape `aggregate`, which on `main` posts `aggregations`, `where` and `groupBy` to the existing data query (`ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts`, the `looksLikeSpecShape` branch).
- **SQL push-down:** the sums run in the database through that aggregate: one call for the plain columns, one more per record-currency code field with `groupBy`. No id materialisation and no in-app join is added. The client sum over the rows on show is gone, which is the SQL-first direction.
- **`buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` is confined** to the section posted in comment 7023388416: three hunks, the `isBody` option doc, the `bodyTablePlacement` doc and the `bodyTablePlacement` body. `synthTabs`, the tab strip, highlights, header, timeline, approvals and attachments are untouched, so nothing here meets #35595's sections.
- **ADR-0035's form side is untouched in code:** no form-derivation file (`attachInlineSubforms`, plugin-form) is in the diff.

Escalated to the maintainer's merge read:

- **Authority.** The supersession of ruling B on #27055 and of the #27069 amendment's clause (1) rests on the maintainer's words as the coordinator quotes them in the card body. Both quotes in the ADR status line match the card verbatim. The card carries no comment from the maintainer's own account; every comment is the fleet's. The hand merge is what ratifies the ADR change.
- **Association children.** ADR-0035's own form-side paragraph names comments, attachments, audit and activity as commonly `master_detail`. Under the new rule each of those is an overview body table by default until its FK says `relatedList: true` or `false`. The dev measured that none of the four in-repo flips is such an association and that no platform object declares `master_detail` (confirmed by reading the tree). HotCRM was not measured, and the card's acceptance names a HotCRM quote.
- **A4 not measured.** No live record page was driven; the live legs ride on the new checklist item `records-forms.master-detail-body-tables`.
- **Skills follow-up owed.** `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` and one eval still teach the `inlineEdit` rule. The PR declares it on its Skills-docs line; it needs a card number before landing closes.
- **"Show all N" has no ceiling.** It reads all N rows in one window. That is the card's own ask (rule 4), so it is not a finding, but nothing bounds N.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 (should-fix) — `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx`, `rolledUpSums`, the `sameRows` test: an absent `summaryOperations.relationshipField` is read as "this list's FK". The engine resolves an absent one to the child's FIRST `lookup` / `master_detail` field that references the parent (`packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts`, the `fkField = cfName; break` scan), and nothing at authoring refuses the omission. So when a child has two FKs to the same parent and the parent's `sum` roll-up omits `relationshipField`, the body table of the FK the engine did not pick draws the other FK's stored roll-up as its own total. That contradicts the amendment's "sums that column over the same rows" and card rule 5. The shape is rare and legal, the figure is wrong with every gate green, and no test covers a two-FK child. Fix: with `relationshipField` absent, grant `sameRows` only when this list's FK is the one the engine would pick (or the child's only FK to the parent), else fall through to the aggregate; add the two-FK case to `RelatedList.bodyTable-27055.test.tsx`.

N1 (nit) — `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`, the `relatedList` describe still opens "true/absent = shown as an auxiliary panel". Taken alone that clause is no longer true for a `master_detail` field. The same string then states the rule correctly and completely ("Absent on a master_detail field, the list is 'primary' by default … absent on a lookup field it is an auxiliary panel"), so a reader of the whole description cannot arrive at the wrong rule, and the accept set and behaviour are unaffected. That makes it wording, not contract. The TSDoc above it received the qualifier in this same hunk and the published describe did not. Rewrite the value table by type ("true = auxiliary panel; absent = 'primary' on a master_detail field, auxiliary on a lookup field") when S1's fix moves the head, or on a follow-up card; it regenerates three reference pages.

N2 (nit) — `docs/adr/0035-config-driven-master-detail.md`, the new note says such a table "sits … under the header strip and above the field sections". It omits that a field group's `relatedList` still positions a table among the sections, and that with no section the details node leads. `bodyTablePlacement` does both, and the `relatedList` TSDoc says the first.

N3 (nit) — the same note cites "§3" for "Only `inlineEdit` children are inlined". ADR-0035 has no numbered sections; the sentence sits under Decision, "Derivation rules". The quotation finds it, the number does not.

N4 (nit) — `RelatedList.tsx`: on the enlarged face a chip (mine, overdue) narrows the rows shown, while the totals line stays the total of the whole list and is labelled only "Total".

By file:

- `docs/adr/0035-config-driven-master-detail.md` — **holds.** The amendment states the supersession accurately and cites both superseded rulings by id: clause (1) of the #27069 note, and ruling B on #27055 as #27478 implemented it. The status line gains a second dated amendment naming the card and the epic; the first amendment's text is left as written, which keeps the history readable. The form side stays intact and consistent: "Only `inlineEdit` children are inlined" is untouched, the note says in terms that a `master_detail` child without `inlineEdit` is a body table on the record page and stays out of the parent's form, and no form code moves. Each sentence about the page was read against the implementing files: the placement (`bodyTablePlacement`, save N2), drawn when empty (the header row and one empty row), and server totals (save S1).
- `packages/spec/src/data/related-list-body-table.ts` — **holds.** The predicate is right against card rule 1 in every cell, and remains the one judgement: `deriveRelatedLists` sets `isPrimary` from it, `RecordDetailView` reads `isBody = isPrimary`, both Studio inspectors and both refusal doors call it, and no implementing file in the diff reads `inlineEdit` to decide body-ness. The header carries #27478, ruling B, #35597 and ADR-0035. The refusal sentence matches the new rule.
- `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` — **agrees** with the predicate in substance (all five cells stated), save N1.
- `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` — **agrees.** The field-group TSDoc and describe both name the new body-table set, and the remedy text is still correct.
- `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` — **agrees.** Unplaced tables lead the field sections in the order given; group-placed tables keep their group position; with no section the details node leads.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts` and `RecordDetailView.tsx` — **agree.** An authored page's `record:related_list` nodes take the body treatment only when the relationship is a body table by the same predicate; a named-page block still yields none.
- `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx` — **agrees** with the totals sentence except S1; the stored roll-up is used only when the list declares no filter, and a data source with no `aggregate` draws no total instead of a client sum.

No must-fix. One should-fix, S1, open on this head.

os-dev-report

**Contract L2 rework round, delta report.** Head `af275005` (was `b4ba2a6d`). Commits: `719ca6f5` S1, `aa146761` N2+N3, `0c84cf7e` N1, `9ad58e75` regenerated references, `af275005` the describe pin the N1 rewrite left red (Test Core 2/10 on `9ad58e75`).

- **S1, done.** `RelatedList.tsx` `rolledUpSums`: a roll-up with no `relationshipField` grants `sameRows` only when this list's key is the engine's pick, the child's FIRST `lookup` / `master_detail` field whose `reference` is the parent (`engineRollUpForeignKey`, the same scan as the engine's summary-index build). A single-key child is the same case. Any other key falls through to the server aggregate. Pinned in `RelatedList.bodyTable-27055.test.tsx`: on a two-key child the engine's key reads the stored roll-up and the other key calls the aggregate with its own key in `where`.
